issues.title: Autopilot control: durable queue, worker leases, recovery and repository maintenance
issues.body:
<!-- dungeon-veil-autopilot-control -->

## Purpose

This issue is the durable coordination, queue, lease, recovery and handoff point for Dungeon Veil autonomous work. GitHub is the source of truth. Chat reports are informational only. Replit is forbidden.

## Active operating model: exactly two regular workers

Dungeon Veil uses exactly two regular ChatGPT automation roles in `Europe/Berlin`. Their actual enabled schedules are external automation state and must be read live; do not hard-code clock times here or infer them from historical comments.

1. **Master implementer** (`worker: primary`)
   - owns the highest-priority free product task;
   - implements, tests, commits, pushes and maintains its PR;
   - creates a risk-based exact-head test plan and inspects the selected evidence;
   - may carry a fully accepted exact head through Ready, merge and publication.
2. **Master verifier** (`worker: verifier`)
   - independently verifies the risk classification, test-plan mapping, exact-head gates, reviews, threads and evidence;
   - expands an understated plan and may safely fix focused defects when no primary scope overlaps;
   - performs final acceptance, Expected-Head merge without auto-merge, retains branches and verifies deployment.

The actual enabled automation configuration is authoritative for execution times. If repository text and live automation state disagree only about schedule, correct the stale documentation; do not change worker scope or create an extra regular worker just to match an old clock time.

There are no active scheduled `secondary` or `visual` workers. Old comments using those worker names are historical records only and do not authorize new work. Do not create additional regular workers unless the user explicitly changes this operating model after concrete evidence that two workers are insufficient.

`worker: background` is permitted only for an explicitly separate, short-lived coordination or migration task. It is never a third scheduled product worker.

## Immutable project rules

- repository: `ys2mm422yb-max/DungeonVeil`
- only target, test and publication branch: `fix/mobile-telegraphs-room-21-50-balance`
- only public test URL: `https://ys2mm422yb-max.github.io/DungeonVeil/`
- never change, target, merge into or publish from `main`
- leave PR #315 untouched
- no auto-merge
- no automatic branch deletion
- no force-push, reset or overwriting another worker's commits
- Playwright retries remain `0`
- do not weaken assertions, coverage, thresholds, acceptance criteria or timeouts
- evidence follows Issue #366 budgets and SHA-256 deduplication
- no temporary GitHub Actions workflows as patch transport

A known defect, rejecting user report, unresolved review requirement, unreviewed visual issue or unmet acceptance criterion blocks Ready and merge.

## Mandatory work order and state machines

Finish existing priority work before opening unnecessary new PRs. Current order is maintained in the newest handoffs below.

Primary state machine:
`IMPLEMENTIEREN -> TESTPLAN -> EXAKT-HEAD-TESTS -> EVIDENCE -> READY -> READY-GATES -> MERGE -> DEPLOY -> DONE`

Verifier state machine:
`VERIFY -> TESTPLAN-REVIEW -> EVIDENCE -> READY-GATES -> MERGE -> DEPLOY -> DONE`

A worker may not report the same exact head, state and blocker for three consecutive runs without a new concrete action. `waiting_external` is not a run-ending condition when independent work is available.

## Live queue discovery

At the start of every pass read this issue and its newest comments, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/ADAPTIVE_TEST_POLICY.md`, roadmap #323, open issues, PRs, reviews, exact-head Actions, artifacts, deployments and current user feedback.

Queue priority:

1. safety, data loss, auth, build, deployment and merge blockers;
2. current exact-head red, cancelled or missing gates;
3. unresolved reviews, active PR defects and rejected user feedback;
4. unfinished acceptance criteria in existing work;
5. visible UI/gameplay/mobile/asset defects;
6. roadmap and remaining backlog;
7. safe test, validator, evidence and process improvements.

Issue #376 and roadmap #323 are coordination sources, not product tasks to close. PR #315 is excluded.

## Lease protocol

Before every GitHub write, create one narrow comment containing `<!-- dungeon-veil-worker-lease -->` with:

- `worker: primary|verifier|background`
- unique `run_id`
- `status: active|released|completed|waiting_external|blocked_external`
- issue, PR, branch, exact head, scope, files, started time, expiry no more than 55 minutes later, and exact resume operation

Before writing:

1. read current leases;
2. reject any overlapping issue, PR, branch, file or scope;
3. claim exactly one narrow exact-head lease;
4. re-read the affected head after claiming;
5. stay inside the declared scope;
6. never hold more than one own active lease;
7. terminalize the lease before the run ends.

Only a current, unexpired, exact-head overlapping lease blocks work. Historical `secondary` and `visual` leases remain audit history but can never be renewed.

## Durable progress memory

Every active-task handoff must include:

- `task_key`
- `state`
- `attempt`
- `exact_head`
- `risk_level`
- `test_plan_status`
- `selected_checks`
- `selected_evidence`
- `omitted_checks_with_reasons`
- `last_completed_step`
- `next_executable_step`
- `artifact_ids`
- `known_good_runs`
- `blocker_class`
- `updated_at`

The next run resumes at `next_executable_step`; it must not restart a broad audit. Local files are not durable memory. Artifact IDs, hashes and run IDs are durable memory.

## Adaptive risk-based testing

The canonical contract is `docs/ADAPTIVE_TEST_POLICY.md`, enforced by `scripts/validate-adaptive-test-plan.mjs`, the permanent Adaptive Test Plan workflow and the PR template.

Every new PR except protected historical PR #315 must document:

- risk level: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `critical`;
- affected domains, files, modes, menus, rooms, states, devices and browsers;
- a concrete proof mapping for every acceptance criterion;
- selected exact-head checks and evidence with technical reasons;
- omitted broad checks with technical non-impact reasons;
- escalation triggers;
- verifier decision: `pending`, `accepted` or `expanded`.

Selection rules:

- `low`: docs/process/non-executable metadata — focused structure or policy validation; no browser/game evidence without executable impact;
- `medium`: localized nonvisual code — focused unit/contract checks plus TypeScript/build where applicable;
- `high`: visible UI, interaction, gameplay, animation, assets, touch, layout or renderer behavior — focused journeys and compact evidence; all four supported portrait projects whenever browser, touch, layout, WebGL, renderer or gameplay differences can matter;
- `critical`: auth/security, Supabase/RLS/RPC, persistence/cloud, economy/rewards, multiplayer/reconnect, world-boss rotation, shared navigation, renderer/WebGL lifecycle, global registries/spawns, deployment or central workflows — full relevant integration, recovery, idempotency, exact-head and cross-device gates.

A run test is required only when the change is visible or functional during a run or creates a plausible run regression. Workers select the exact menus, rooms, states and devices that prove the changed contract instead of performing an unrelated generic tour.

Adaptive selection never permits weakening quality. Explicit issue, review or user-required checks stay mandatory. A relevant red, cancelled, stale or missing gate cannot be reclassified as irrelevant after failure. The verifier independently checks the diff and plan and must expand or reject understated coverage.

Evidence must be small, separate, manifest-backed, SHA-256-deduplicated and directly tied to acceptance criteria. Every relevant hash-distinct screenshot, video, trace or runtime artifact must actually be opened before acceptance.

## WIP and failure classification

Across the two workers, keep at most one actively modified/verified product PR plus one additional cleanly parked `waiting_external` PR. Do not open a third implementation PR while active work can continue.

Classify blockers as:

- `product`: reproducible code, test, workflow, data, UI, gameplay or evidence defect; fix it or create a precise focused handoff
- `transient_tool`: container, network, DNS, cache, connector or runtime failure; try two technically different methods, then perform other concrete work
- `external_wait`: unchanged running GitHub job or unavailable external resource; park it and continue elsewhere

Only `product` is a functional PR blocker. The same transient tool error in two consecutive runs requires one deduplicated process issue and, when safely isolatable, a permanent workflow/evidence fix.

## Quality, merge and publication

- keep PR head/base/draft/ready status and descriptions factual;
- require a valid adaptive test-plan block before Ready;
- inspect and resolve actionable review threads;
- actually open relevant hash-distinct screenshots, videos, traces and runtime evidence;
- verify unchanged exact head, base, mergeability, reviews, threads, test-plan validity, selected and otherwise applicable required checks, artifacts, leases and every task criterion immediately before Ready or merge;
- merge only after all applicable Draft and Ready exact-head gates are green and no known blocker remains;
- use Expected-Head protection, never auto-merge, and retain the source branch;
- keep issues open until their complete Definition of Done is satisfied;
- verify the target-branch Pages deployment after every merge.

A browser, DNS, cache, network or tool inability to open the public URL alone does not block merge when every applicable exact-head gate is green, evidence is accepted and the exact merged target commit has a successful Pages deployment. A failed, missing or stale deployment remains a blocker.

## Current work

The two regular workers record active assignments, terminal states, exact heads, adaptive test plans, evidence and resume operations in comments below. Historical four-worker records remain for audit history but are no longer operational instructions.

issues.title: [outage] LML prod hit 'Too many open files' on 2026-05-01 ~21:44 UTC
issues.body:
## Symptom

Around **2026-05-01 21:44 UTC** LML production stopped accepting connections. Symptoms from caller side:

- `GET /health` → connection timeout (no response)
- `POST /api/v1/lookup` → 502 from Railway edge (`Application failed to respond`, request_id `_eeKiKR_TlOlwRcYxtoGcA`)
- request-o-matic `/health/ready` flipped to `lookup: timeout`
- iOS-app `/request` calls returned 502 to DJs

## Root cause

`OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files`. Captured from `railway logs --environment production --service library-metadata-lookup` immediately before the recovery redeploy:

```
2026-05-01 21:44:53,889 - asyncio - ERROR - socket.accept() out of system resource
socket: <asyncio.TransportSocket fd=7, family=2, type=1, proto=6, laddr=('0.0.0.0', 8080)>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/asyncio/selector_events.py", line 178, in _accept_connection
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/socket.py", line 295, in accept
OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files
```

Identical traceback repeated every few ms — the process was stuck in an `accept()` retry loop, unable to open new sockets.

## Recovery

A no-op env-var change (`FORCE_RESTART=<timestamp>`) triggered a redeploy that swapped to a fresh container. After the cutover (~30s), `/health` returned 200 and `POST /api/v1/lookup` returned 200 in 1.3s. iOS app traffic restored.

## Why this matters

This is not transient — it's a leak. The container had been running long enough to exhaust its FD limit, and unless the leak source is fixed, the next instance will trip the same wall. It will keep happening on a clock until something changes.

## Suspect surfaces

A few obvious places to investigate, in order of likelihood:

1. **`asyncpg` connection pool to discogs-cache and musicbrainz-cache.** If a code path opens connections without returning them to the pool (or creates new pools per-request instead of sharing), each leaked connection holds an FD.
2. **`httpx.AsyncClient` instances.** Unclosed clients keep their underlying transport / connection pool alive. Look for ad-hoc `httpx.AsyncClient()` not behind a context manager or shared singleton.
3. **Spotify / Bandcamp / Deezer / Apple Music streaming-check clients.** Concurrent fan-out without bounded connection pools could spike FDs under load.
4. **The external-cache fallback paths added in Phase 1.5 mojibake recovery** — discogs-cache + musicbrainz-cache trigram queries route through new asyncpg paths.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Add an `/admin/fd-count` debug endpoint (or just log `len(os.listdir('/proc/self/fd'))` on every request) so we can graph FD growth over time and correlate to traffic patterns.
- [ ] Add a Sentry breadcrumb / metric tagged with FD count on `/health` to catch creep early.
- [ ] Audit every `httpx.AsyncClient` and `asyncpg.create_pool` call site; ensure they're shared singletons with clean shutdown.
- [ ] Consider raising the container's FD soft limit in the Dockerfile as a backstop, but that just delays the next outage — fix the leak.

## Severity

**High.** This took down the iOS app's request feature with no caller-side error (request-o-matic surfaces 502s, but the iOS `Sentry` breadcrumb just shows `bad gateway` with no upstream attribution). Recovery requires manual intervention; auto-restart on FD exhaustion would help but doesn't replace fixing the leak.

## Cross-references

- Related to but distinct from the 2026-05-01 LML auth incident (#98 in WXYC/request-o-matic). That was resolved earlier today; this is a new failure mode that surfaced 2 hours later.

issues.title: [BUG] CORE — Flaky allegro-order-sync-e2e int-spec: OrderCreateContendedException on a single, non-concurrent lock acquire
issues.body:
## Problem / Context

`apps/worker/test/integration/allegro-order-sync-e2e.int-spec.ts` › `Complete Order Sync Flow` › `should sync orders from poll to order processor` fails intermittently in CI with:

```
SyncJobExecutionError: Marketplace order sync failed: Order create is contended for order ol_order_... (destinationConnectionId=dest-prestashop-1); a concurrent create holds the lock — retry
  at MarketplaceOrderSyncHandler.execute (apps/worker/src/sync/handlers/marketplace-order-sync.handler.ts:50:13)
Cause:
OrderCreateContendedException: ...
  at OrderSyncService.createOrderIdempotently (libs/core/src/orders/application/services/order-sync.service.ts:211:13)
```

Observed twice on 2026-08-31, on two unrelated PRs whose diffs never touch `orders`/`sync` code:
- https://github.com/openlinker-project/openlinker/actions/runs/33380848241/job/99452698826 (PR #2700, frontend-only diff)
- https://github.com/openlinker-project/openlinker/actions/runs/33381044654/job/99453345457 (PR #2710)

`OrderCreateContendedException` is thrown from `createOrderIdempotently` (`libs/core/src/orders/application/services/order-sync.service.ts:211`) when `SyncLockPort.acquire()` returns `null` — i.e. Redis's `SET key val NX PX ttl` did not set the key because it already existed.

**What's already ruled out** (investigated 2026-08-31, see PR discussion):
- `WORKER_RUNNER_ENABLED=false` and `WORKER_INTAKE_ENABLED=false` are both set by `apps/worker/test/jest-global-setup.cjs` for every integration run, so no background `SyncJobRunner` poll loop or `JobIntakeConsumer` stream loop is alive to independently re-process the enqueued job concurrently with the test's own explicit `orderSyncHandler.execute(...)` call.
- The test's `listCapabilityAdapters` mock returns exactly **one** `OrderProcessorManager` destination (`dest-prestashop-1`), so `OrderSyncService.syncOrder`'s `Promise.allSettled(destinations.map(...))` fans out to exactly one `createOrderIdempotently` call — there is no second concurrent caller *within* this test's own code path.
- The internal order id (`ol_order_<uuid>`) is minted via `IdentifierMappingService.getOrCreateInternalId` → `generateInternalId`, which is `randomUUID()`-based, not deterministic — so a lock-key collision with a *stale* lock left by an unrelated earlier test (in this file or another `*.int-spec.ts` sharing the same Testcontainers Redis instance) is statistically implausible.
- `RedisSyncLockService.acquire` (`libs/core/src/sync/application/services/redis-sync-lock.service.ts:22`) is a single `SET NX PX` call with no retry loop of its own — so there's no code-visible mechanism at that layer for a caller to race against itself.
- Ran locally with Docker: `allegro-order-sync-e2e.int-spec.ts` alone (4/4 runs green) and the full 17-suite `apps/worker` integration run (17/17 green, including this test) both pass reliably. **The flake does not reproduce locally** — it appears to be specific to CI runner conditions (resource contention / Redis round-trip latency under load).

**Leading, unconfirmed hypothesis**: under CI-runner network/scheduling pressure, something causes `acquire()` to observe its *own* prior (successful) `SET NX` as a conflict — e.g. a slow/retried round trip to the Testcontainers Redis. This has not been proven; it needs runtime evidence from a reproduction, not just a code read.

## Proposed Solution

Two independent tracks — do the defensive fix regardless of whether the exact mechanism is ever nailed down, because it strictly improves lock correctness under network uncertainty:

1. **Harden `RedisSyncLockService.acquire`** (`libs/core/src/sync/application/services/redis-sync-lock.service.ts`): when `SET NX PX` reports the key already exists, `GET` it and compare the stored value against the token this call just generated (or, better, mint the token from a stable per-call input and check-before-generate) — if a resent/duplicate request from this exact call already won the key, treat it as "acquired by us" rather than raising contention. This is standard defensive practice for `SET NX`-based locks and would eliminate self-inflicted contention regardless of transport cause. Add a unit test in `redis-sync-lock.service.spec.ts` covering the self-recognition path.
2. **If (1) doesn't kill the flake**, add temporary diagnostic logging around `SyncLockPort.acquire`/`release` calls (key, token, timestamp, caller) scoped to CI-only (e.g. an env flag), run the suite a few times in CI until it reproduces, and use the captured timeline to find the actual second writer.

Do not attempt to "fix" this by increasing timeouts or retry counts blindly — that would mask rather than resolve whatever is actually happening.

## Classification

**Type**: CORE
**Layer**: Application (`SyncLockPort` / `RedisSyncLockService`), Testing (`apps/worker/test/integration/allegro-order-sync-e2e.int-spec.ts`)
**File(s)**:
- `libs/core/src/sync/application/services/redis-sync-lock.service.ts`
- `libs/core/src/orders/application/services/order-sync.service.ts`
- `apps/worker/test/integration/allegro-order-sync-e2e.int-spec.ts`

## Dependencies

- None

## Assumptions

- The failure is CI-environment-specific (network/timing under load), not a logic bug reachable in production traffic patterns — this is inferred from non-reproduction locally (isolated + full-suite runs), not confirmed by a captured CI reproduction.
- Fixing `acquire()` to be idempotent against its own resent request is safe and matches the port's existing token-based compare-and-delete/extend pattern already used by `release`/`extend`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `RedisSyncLockService.acquire` no longer raises contention against a request that actually won its own lock (self-recognition on retry/duplicate).
- [ ] Unit test added for the self-recognition path in `redis-sync-lock.service.spec.ts`.
- [ ] `allegro-order-sync-e2e.int-spec.ts` passes on CI across at least 5 consecutive CI runs of the same PR (or documented evidence the flake is resolved/root-caused another way).
- [ ] If root cause is found to be something other than lock self-collision, this issue is updated with the real cause before closing.
- [ ] No architecture boundary violations (CORE ↔ Integration).

issues.title: Go runtime suite fails a different test on each CI attempt
issues.body:
The Go runtime suite is failing intermittently on `main`-based PR runs, on a **different test each attempt**. Observed on PR #403 — a control-plane-only change touching no file under `internal/` — run 33372425990:

- attempt 1: `--- FAIL: TestServiceStatusCancellationAndRepeatedCallsLeakNothing` (`internal/install`, 1.21s)
- attempt 2: `--- FAIL: TestSupervisorPersistsOuterRunnerExitNotProviderExit`

The `control-plane` job passed on both attempts, and on every earlier run of the same branch. A deterministic break fails the same test twice; two different tests across two attempts of the same commit is flakiness.

This is not one of the two already recorded. Those are the `test-local-ci-lease.sh` timeout under load, and `managed_no_op_rejects_an_unrelated_same_version_responder` reporting `reloaded` where `unchanged` was expected. Both tests failing here are process- and lifecycle-sensitive, which is the same family.

Impact: `checks` and `required` are required statuses, so an unrelated pull request cannot merge without repeated reruns. That erodes the signal — a red run stops being evidence, which is the property the gate exists to provide.

Worth establishing first: whether `main`'s own-branch runs are also red. That separates "flaky under merge-ref composition" from "flaky everywhere", and the two have different fixes.

Found while using the Maintainer App to diagnose its own PR, via `observe_pull_request_workflows` and `read_pull_request_job_log`.

issues.title: Three tests assert exact teardown state, so CI fails intermittently
issues.body:
Three tests assert the exact instantaneous state of an asynchronous teardown, so they fail intermittently on hosted runners and pass on a quiet local Mac. Same mistake, three places — not three unrelated flakes, and not an unreliable environment.

Observed on PR #403, whose diff touches no file under `internal/`:

| run / attempt | test | assertion that failed |
|---|---|---|
| 33372425990 / 1 | `TestServiceStatusCancellationAndRepeatedCallsLeakNothing` | `service_darwin_test.go:620: goroutines = 2, want 3` |
| 33372425990 / 2 | `TestSupervisorPersistsOuterRunnerExitNotProviderExit` | `supervisor_darwin_test.go:802: RunNext: EOF` / `runner: invalid lifecycle state` / `runner: frame header: write attempt-daemon-control: broken pipe` |
| 33372425990 / 3 | — passed on the identical tree — | |
| 33411568025 / 1 | `TestServerRequiresRequestEOFBeforedispatch` | `server_test.go:397: close unix ->…/runtimes/factory.sock: shutdown: socket is not connected` |

`control-plane` passed on every run.

What each is actually asserting:

- **An exact live goroutine count.** `goroutines = 2, want 3` means one had not been scheduled yet, or had already exited. A leak check that reads an instantaneous count without synchronising against the goroutines it is counting is measuring the scheduler, not a leak. Leak detection wants a bounded wait for the count to settle, or a handle on the goroutines themselves.
- **A clean control-pipe write during shutdown.** `broken pipe` on `attempt-daemon-control` with `invalid lifecycle state` is the peer going away mid-write. That is a legal outcome of the teardown being raced, not a defect the test means to catch.
- **A clean socket close.** `shutdown: socket is not connected` is `ENOTCONN` — the peer closed first. On a unix socket that is normal, and treating `Close` returning it as a failure asserts an ordering the runtime does not promise.

Two consequences worth separating. Operationally, `checks` and `required` are required statuses, so an unrelated change needs two or three attempts to merge, and a red run stops carrying information — the one property the gate exists to provide. Substantively, if any of these three teardowns is *meant* to be deterministic, then the intermittent failure is evidence of a real runtime race and the test is right to be unhappy; that distinction has to be settled per test before any of them is relaxed.

A note on diagnosing this: `read_pull_request_job_log` returns the full 64 KiB tail, and the assertion messages sit in it. Filtering the log to lines matching `FAIL` discards exactly the line that names the cause, which is how this first got recorded as "flaky" with no mechanism. Read the lines around `--- FAIL`, not the matching lines.

Also note `#349`'s signature (`lockf: descriptor: already locked`, `run_pending_traps: bad value in trap_list[15]`, children reaped at 137) appears in these logs while the lease phase itself reports `local-ci lease tests passed`. It is noise here and easy to misattribute.

issues.title: Flaky CI: the full-form integrity spec fails intermittently under load
issues.body:
### Problem

`integrity/60-content-integrity-full-form.cy.ts` fails CI intermittently, and it failed twice on 2026-08-31 alone — each time turning an otherwise green PR run red, on heads whose diffs could not plausibly cause it:

- **Run [33396262985](https://github.com/Jahia/formidable/actions/runs/33396262985)** (PR #233, head `8ca430f`): `AssertionError: Timed out retrying after 30000ms: form island hydrated: expected false to equal true` — the live page rendered but the island never hydrated within 30s.
- **Run [33407936589](https://github.com/Jahia/formidable/actions/runs/33407936589)** (PR #234, head `8b5b4d8`): `CypressError: cy.visit() failed … Error: ESOCKETTIMEDOUT` on the live page — the server did not answer at all within the socket timeout. The *previous* head of the same PR (`8a80b62`, one cosmetic spec change earlier) had passed the identical suite 75 minutes before.

The two failures have different shapes (slow hydration vs. no HTTP response) but the same signature: the server is momentarily too slow around this spec. It is plausibly the heaviest case of the suite — a full two-step form with every field type, a live visit with hydration, a complete submission with file upload, plus two content-integrity scans — and it runs late in the suite, when the instance has accumulated the most load.

### Impact

Any PR can go red for reasons unrelated to its diff; every occurrence costs a ~40-minute rerun and erodes trust in the suite (a red run no longer means a broken PR).

### Evidence for triage

- Spec: `tests/cypress/e2e/integrity/60-content-integrity-full-form.cy.ts`
- The spec is retry-safe: its fixture names are `Date.now()`-suffixed, so a retry attempt does not collide with the nodes of the failed attempt.

issues.title: [YSQL] TestPgRegressParallelPlans#schedule: parallel index only scan case flips to serial after the parallel_setup_cost increase
issues.body:
Jira Link: [DB-23242](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-23242)
## Summary

`org.yb.pgsql.TestPgRegressParallelPlans#schedule` started failing on `master` at build 2.31.0.0-b391, commit e6c4a12aa01feb36f1a164d35a1448e6a052be31, "[#33413] YSQL: Re-increase parallel_setup_cost to compensate parallel row count fix", which raised `YB_DEFAULT_PARALLEL_SETUP_COST` from 1700.0 to 4080.0 in `src/postgres/src/include/optimizer/cost.h`.

One pre-existing case in `yb.orig.parallel_plans` now sits on the serial/parallel cost boundary and flips between runs. #33413 regenerated `yb.orig.parallel_plans.out` only for the three new batched nested loop join cases it added, so this case still expects the parallel plan.

- Failing build types: alma8-clang21-release, arm-alma8-clang21-release.  The test does not run on the tsan or asan configs.
- Stability: https://csiweb.dev.yugabyte.com/stability/test?branch=master&uid=org.yb.pgsql.TestPgRegressParallelPlans%23schedule

## Failure reason

```
pg_regress exited with error code: 1, failed tests: [yb.orig.parallel_plans]
regression.diffs:
diff -U3 ${TEST_TMPDIR}/pgregress_output/yb_parallel_plans_schedule/expected/yb.orig.parallel_plans.out ${TEST_TMPDIR}/pgregress_output/yb_parallel_plans_schedule/results/yb.orig.parallel_plans.out
@@ -286,13 +286,11 @@
 --
 EXPLAIN (COSTS off, SUMMARY off)
 SELECT k1, k2, k3 FROM t1m t WHERE k3 BETWEEN 5000-(900/2 - 1) AND 5000+(900/2);
-                        QUERY PLAN
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Gather
-   Workers Planned: 2
-   ->  Parallel Index Only Scan using t1m_k1k2k3 on t1m t
-         Index Cond: ((k3 >= 4551) AND (k3 <= 5450))
-(4 rows)
+                  QUERY PLAN
+-----------------------------------------------
+ Index Only Scan using t1m_k1k2k3 on t1m t
+   Index Cond: ((k3 >= 4551) AND (k3 <= 5450))
+(2 rows)

 --
 -- Should choose PARALLEL append + gather plan
```

This is the only hunk, and it is byte for byte identical across every affected run.  The case sits under an explicit intent header in the test source:

```
--
-- Should choose PARALLEL index only scan
--
```

## Regression range

| build | commit | alma8-clang21-release | arm-alma8-clang21-release |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| b388 to b390 | up to a139655f2df010bc8e81137f880dc4ecb8fc2981 | PASSED | PASSED |
| b391 | e6c4a12aa01feb36f1a164d35a1448e6a052be31 | PASSED | FAILED |
| b392 | not run | - | - |
| b393 | c33e394f6352e6b0e1f87d4c428f19edafa8600c | FAILED | FAILED |
| b394 | 99a16cd3e179d2e97629d2173a8738e11ff76338 | FAILED (unrelated, see below) | PASSED |
| b395 | 4c8134c85ad5948bc7a10d9c4882f88fdaae4e4f | PASSED | FAILED |

Attributable to this issue: 4 failures in the 8 runs from b391 onward.  The 15 builds before b391 were green on both configs, 30 consecutive passing runs.

The b390 to b391 range contains six commits.  The five besides e6c4a12aa01feb36f1a164d35a1448e6a052be31 are a docs OS support table fix, a YBA pgaudit alert fix, a CDC stale workflow removal, a thirdparty curl bump, and a YBA CLI client fix.  None of them touch the planner.

## Why it is intermittent rather than deterministic

At 900 rows the `k3` range is close enough to the serial/parallel crossover that after the 2.4x setup cost increase the ANALYZE sampling variation between runs decides which plan wins.  That is why b391 and b395 still passed on x86_64 and b394 passed on aarch64.

## Suggested fix

Widen the `k3` range so the parallel plan wins with margin, keeping the case consistent with its "Should choose PARALLEL index only scan" header.  #33413 sized its own new cases this way, picking 160 rows for the serial batched nested loop join case and 330 rows for the parallel one.

Simply regenerating the expected output to `Index Only Scan` would contradict the header and would leave a case that can flap back to the parallel plan.

## Failure that is not this issue

The b394 alma8-clang21-release failure has a completely different diff, a series of `IO error: ... rejected. Node ... has insufficient disk space` write rejections during the `t1m` load, followed by cascading `relation "t10k" does not exist` errors.  That is the CI worker running out of filesystem space and is unrelated to the plan flip.

## Prior history

Not to be confused with #32597, which covered memory, disk, and stale plan flakiness in the same test and was fixed at build b374 by 88d893b72f174417d2d4de99f71e799f071658d4.  That fix held green from b374 through b390.

The parallel divisor row estimate change that #33413 was compensating for is cbdd7ba6f8fb56959f6bb2df9e9e64cf86e000b8.

## Failing runs

- b391 arm-alma8-clang21-release: https://csi.dev.yugabyte.com/ui/#dbft/launches/17196/162997/729618973/730068056/log
- b393 alma8-clang21-release: https://csi.dev.yugabyte.com/ui/#dbft/launches/17242/163358/731456770/732202787/log
- b393 arm-alma8-clang21-release: https://csi.dev.yugabyte.com/ui/#dbft/launches/17242/163359/731223343/731332441/log
- b395 arm-alma8-clang21-release: https://csi.dev.yugabyte.com/ui/#dbft/launches/17272/163610/733042082/733091944/log

## Environment details

- Branch `master`, version 2.31.0.0.
- First failing commit e6c4a12aa01feb36f1a164d35a1448e6a052be31, build 2.31.0.0-b391, 2026-08-26.
- Last commit green on both configs: a139655f2df010bc8e81137f880dc4ecb8fc2981, build 2.31.0.0-b390.
- Build types: alma8-clang21-release on x86_64 and arm-alma8-clang21-release on aarch64.  Both are release builds, so the plan flip is not a debug build artifact.
- OS: AlmaLinux 8.  The aarch64 workers report `Linux 4.18.0-553.124.4.el8_10.aarch64`, AWS us-west-2.
- Cluster topology: MiniYBCluster, 3 masters and 3 tservers on a single host, RF 3, `--memory_limit_hard_bytes=1073741824` per node, `--yb_num_shards_per_tserver=1`.  The test runs against a colocated database with `yb_enable_optimizer_statistics=on`, `yb_enable_base_scans_cost_model=on`, `yb_fetch_row_limit=0`, `yb_fetch_size_limit=1MB`, `yb_parallel_range_rows=10000`, and `yb_parallel_range_size=1MB`.


[DB-23242]: https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-23242?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
